movesets.name: Offensive
movesets.description:
• Great Tusk's primal physical prowess and great support options make it a good choice for a bulky Fighting-type.

  • Earthquake versus Headlong Rush: Headlong Rush's defensive drops and vulnerability to Rocky Helmet make it a riskier option than Earthquake, but the extra power OHKOes maximum HP Gholdengo.

  • Ice Spinner: This is highly recommended to avoid getting walled by Dragonite before it Terastallizes, while also dealing good damage to common Tera Flying Pokemon such as Gholdengo and Kingambit.

  • Rapid Spin: Great Tusk is one of the best Rapid Spin users, being able to take advantage of it offensively and heavily pressuring Ting-Lu to Terastallize or switch out.

  • Knock Off: Beyond the usefulness of removing items, this is Great Tusk's best move against Air Balloon Gholdengo.

Other Options

  • Rock Tomb: Rock Tomb is a good speed control option, great for breaking through Dragonite's Multiscale while nullifying its potential Speed boost, while letting other teammates take advantage of speed control. It also lets Great Tusk hit troublesome Focus Sash Ghost-types such as Flutter Mane and Gengar, something Rapid Spin can't do.

  • Iron Head: If using Tera Steel, Iron Head is a decent option for OHKOing Flutter Mane without using Headlong Rush, and it deals heavy damage to Baxcalibur and Tera Fairy Rotom-W.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Medium: Terastallization can help with Great Tusk's poor special bulk by resisting certain hits, but it works fine without it.

  • Steel: Tera Steel greatly aids against the many Fairy-, Ice-, and Flying-types that would otherwise prey on Great Tusk, such as Mimikyu, Iron Bundle, and Tera Flying Dragonite.

  • Water: Tera Water massively improves the matchup against Chien-Pao, and can let Great Tusk survive an encounter with offensive Iron Moth or Chi-Yu that lack Choice Specs.

  • Ground: The furious increase in power Tera Ground provides can be useful late game, giving Earthquake a high chance to OHKO even defensive Gholdengo and Headlong Rush the ability to 2HKO Terastallized Skeledirge.

  • Fighting: Not only does Tera Fighting improve the Chien-Pao matchup, but it OHKOs even the bulkiest Ting-Lu with Close Combat.

Items

  • Assault Vest: This patches up Great Tusk's poor Special Defense, which can be paired with the correct Tera Type to help against foes like Iron Bundle, Flutter Mane, Iron Moth, and Chi-Yu.

  • Booster Energy: When saving Great Tusk for late-game sweeps, Booster Energy is preferred over Life Orb for preserving its HP against priority attacks.

  • Focus Sash: Focus Sash on such a bulky Pokemon may seem wasteful, but it vastly improves Great Tusk's matchups against special attackers such as Rotom-W and makes setting up Stealth Rock a far simpler task. If using Focus Sash, consider using the first alternate EV spread below.

Alternate EV Spreads
  • 4 HP / 12 Def / 236 Atk / 252 Spe with Jolly: This EV spread survives Adamant Focus Sash Meowscarada's Flower Trick followed by Sucker Punch, making it a good spread to use if using Focus Sash and Rapid Spin.
Assault Vest EV Spreads

  • All of these EV spreads will at least avoid a 2HKO from Modest Flutter Mane's Mystical Fire if using Tera Steel. If using a different Tera type, 16 Special Defense EVs can be redistributed.

  • 52 HP / 148 Atk / 4 Def / 164 SpD / 140 Spe with Adamant: This EV spread outspeeds Adamant Breloom, and the rare Timid Abomasnow.

  • 4 HP / 44 Atk / 4 Def / 164 SpD / 244 Spe with Adamant: This EV spread is for Rapid Spin, outspeeding Iron Bundle after a Speed boost.

movesets.name: Bulk Up
movesets.description:
• Great Tusk's fantastic Defense stat makes it a great option for setting up Bulk Up late-game.

  • Taunt versus Substitute: Taunt preys on defensive Pokemon such as Wo-Chien and Corviknight, while Substitute protects Great Tusk from Garganacl's Salt Cure. Dragon Tail from Garchomp and Dragonite, and OHKO moves from the likes of Dondozo and Kingambit.

  • Ice Spinner: Dragonite is such a problematic foe that hitting it hard is worth more than a Fighting-type STAB move.

Other Options

  • Body Press: Although it is difficult to fit in without sacrificing utility or coverage, Body Press is a reasonable option if a Fighting-type STAB move is needed.

  • Close Combat: Close Combat does not gel well with the defensive nature of this set, but it deals far more damage to Ting-Lu than any of Great Tusk's other options.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Medium: Great Tusk is a good bulky sweeper on its own, but Terstallization makes it far more difficult to revenge kill.

  • Water: Not only is Tera Water an excellent option against Chien-Pao and Chi-Yu, but it also means Dondozo will never break Great Tusk's Substitute with Wave Crash, and Assault Vest Azumarill become an easy target to set up on.

  • Steel: Tera Steel is a great option for dealing with Great Tusk's weaknesses, such as Fairy-types and makes Iron Bundle usually fail to 2HKO specially defensive Great Tusk without Choice Specs.

  • Poison: Tera Poison is a decent alternative to Tera Steel, providing the vital Fairy-type resistance without the weaknesses to Fighting- and Fire-type attacks and an extremely useful immunity to being poisoned that eases the match-up against Toxic Spikes foes such as Clodsire and Meowscarada.

  • Fire: Fire is not a great defensive type; however, not only does it do well against Fairy-types such as Flutter Mane, it also protects Great Tusk from fast Will-O-Wisp users such as Dragapult, Mimikyu, and Volcarona.

Items

  • Leftovers: The residual recovery from Leftovers best suits the slow set-up of this set, especially if using Substitute.

  • Booster Energy: Depending on the EV spread, Booster Energy can boost Attack or Speed to increase Great Tusk's late-game cleaning potential.

  • Covert Cloak: If a Garganacl check is desperately needed, Covert Cloak Great Tusk is up for the task.

EV Spreads

  • 188 HP / 140 Atk / 4 Def / 36 SpD / 140 Spe with Adamant: This EV spread outspeeds Adamant Breloom and the rare Timid Abomasnow, survives Timid Iron Bundle's Freeze-Dry, and has a very good chance of avoiding a 2HKO from Adamant Azumarill after using Bulk Up. The Attack EVs OHKO Chien-Pao and defensive Gholdengo with Earthquake after Bulk Up.

  • 4 HP / 252 SpD / 252 Spe with Jolly: This spread gains a Speed boost from Protosynthesis, making Great Tusk an even better late-game sweeper at the cost of physical bulk.

  • 244 HP / 20 Atk / 84 Def / 20 SpD / 140 Spe with Impish: This EV spread is meant for use with Tera Steel or Tera Poison, maintaining Great Tusk's Substitute against Dondozo's Wave Crash after Terastallization. It also outspeeds Adamant Breloom and the rare Timid Abomasnow, and survives Timid Iron Bundle's Freeze-Dry.

  • 252 HP / 4 Atk / 252 SpD with Careful: Maximum investment in special bulk makes Great Tusk much more difficult to revenge kill with the likes of Gholdengo and Iron Bundle. The 4 Attack EVs gives an Attack boost from Protosynthesis, which is preferred for improving the Skeledirge matchup and sweeping more easily.

movesets.name: Choice Item
movesets.description:
• Great Tusk's high power attacks make it a fine Choice item holder.

  • Headlong Rush versus Earthquake: Headlong Rush is preferred for stampeding over maximum HP Gholdengo, but Earthquake avoids chip damage from Rocky Helmet and makes Great Tusk far less vulnerable to priority attacks from foes like Dragonite, Chien-Pao, and Palafin-H.

  • Ice Spinner: Great Tusk should never leave its cave without a move to hit Dragonite hard!

  • Knock Off: Knock Off deals massive damage to Air Balloon Gholdengo and is almost guaranteed to OHKO offensive Dragapult after Stealth Rock damage.

  • Jolly versus Adamant: A Jolly nature ensures that Great Tusk outspeeds Gholdengo, and Choice Scarf variants outspeed Dragapult. Adamant is still a reasonable option for more power since Great Tusk will still outpace Breloom, and if using Choice Scarf, Iron Bundle, Flutter Mane, and Chien-Pao.

Other Options
  • Iron Head: If using Tera Steel, this is a reasonable option over Knock Off if Tera Fairy Rotom-W is an issue.
Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Low: While Terastallization can help it clean more easily, it's not an important aspect of this set otherwise.

  • Ground: Tera Ground is the best option for late-game cleaning, dealing significant damage to Dondozo and OHKOing Dragapult with Headlong Rush.

  • Fighting: Tera Fighting threatens to 2HKO Corviknight, an otherwise decent check to Great Tusk, and OHKO even the bulkiest Ting-Lu.

  • Steel: While Great Tusk's special bulk is mediocre, Tera Steel can prevent it from being OHKOed by foes such as Iron Bundle and Flutter Mane.

Items

  • Choice Scarf: Since it outspeeds other major Choice Scarf Pokemon such as Gholdengo and Rotom-W, Great Tusk makes for a good revenge killer.

  • Choice Band: Choice Band is a more niche option due to being extremely vulnerable to revenge kills, but does a much better job of wall-breaking, with Tera boosted Great Tusk even being able to 2HKO a maximum Defense Dondozo with Close Combat or Headlong Rush!

strategies.comments:
Other Options

Wandering Spirit is a niche ability on physically defensive sets that prevents Regenerator Pokemon like Swampert and Roaring Moon from regaining their HP when they pivot out while also letting Great Tusk gain Regenerator. Magic Guard + Life Orb is a great combination for offensive sets, as this prevents Great Tusk from being chipped down by Rocky Helmet and poison from Malignant Chain or Toxic Spikes; it also lets Great Tusk make use of Supercell Slam to hit Corviknight and Skarmory as well as Head Smash for Zapdos and Moltres without taking any recoil. Mold Breaker is used on offensive sets to allow Great Tusk to bypass Fluffy used on Pokemon like Corviknight, Skarmory, and Great Tusk as well as Levitate and Earth Eater on Gholdengo and Pecharunt. Earth Eater gives Great Tusk immunity to Earthquake from Ting-Lu, Swampert, and opposing Great Tusk while also letting it counter Sandy Shocks. Great Tusk can opt for an EV spread of 252 HP / 4 Atk / 252 Spe to make it a fast utility Pokemon while still retaining its defensive prowess. Eject Button is a niche item that swings the momentum in your favor against Pokemon trying to pivot out with U-turn such as Roaring Moon and Corviknight.

Checks and Counters

Special Attackers: Great Tusk's incredibly low Special Defense makes it prone to being OHKOed by special attackers like Deoxys-S, Zapdos, Scream Tail, Gholdengo, and Iron Moth.

Physical Attackers With Super Effective Moves: Chien-Pao, Iron Boulder, Meowscarada, and the Ogerpon formes can all 2HKO Great Tusk with their super effective attacks.

Residual Damage: Residual damage like poison, Spikes, and Rocky Helmet all slowly chip away at Great Tusk, which is compounded by it lacking any sort of longevity if it isn't using Regenerator or Leftovers.

movesets.name: Physically Defensive
movesets.description:
Thanks to its enormous physical bulk, solid utility options, and wide variety of abilities it can use, Great Tusk functions as an excellent physical wall. Earthquake lets Great Tusk hit foes that would otherwise beat it like Pecharunt, Scream Tail, and defensive Gholdengo, whereas Body Press does more damage than Earthquake due to its defensive investment and does solid damage to non-Fluffy Corviknight and Skarmory. Knock Off allows Great Tusk to annoy switch-ins like Corviknight, Skarmory, and opposing Great Tusk by removing their items, while Ice Spinner does good damage to Zapdos. Rapid Spin allows Great Tusk to support its teammates by removing entry hazards. Stealth Rock lets Great Tusk residually chip Pokemon like Chien-Pao, Deoxys-S, and Heatran, while Taunt prevents Corviknight from using Defog, Skarmory from setting up hazards, and both of them from recovering with Roost. Scrappy lets Great Tusk use Rapid Spin against Ghost-types such as Gholdengo and Pecharunt while also being able to hit Gholdengo with Body Press; however, Regenerator gives Great Tusk longevity, which lets it check Roaring Moon and opposing Great Tusk without being scared of getting chipped down, but this means that Great Tusk is forced to be used with non-RegenVest special walls. Alternatively, Fluffy makes Great Tusk incredibly bulky, letting it easily switch in on Choice Band Zamazenta and Roaring Moon. Leftovers is appreciated on Scrappy and Fluffy sets, as Great Tusk lacks longevity, but Rocky Helmet is also an option to punish Corviknight, opposing Great Tusk, Zamazenta, and non-Magic Guard Roaring Moon. Heavy-Duty Boots is a bit more niche, but it lets Great Tusk remove hazards without being affected by them.

Defensive Great Tusk is most often used on bulky offense or balance teams. Attackers that are easily chipped down by entry hazards like Chien-Pao, Deoxys-S, and non-Magic Guard Roaring Moon appreciate Great Tusk removing them with Rapid Spin. Teammates like Zapdos, Roaring Moon, and Iron Moth enjoy the Stealth Rock that Great Tusk sets up, as they can pivot out to slowly chip away at switch-ins such as Corviknight and RegenVest Roaring Moon. Great Tusk's low Special Defense requires special walls like RegenVest Manaphy, Swampert, and Roaring Moon as well as Heatran, Iron Treads, and Empoleon for Regenerator variants of Great Tusk. Great Tusk is also vulnerable to physical attackers like Chien-Pao, Iron Boulder, Meowscarada, and the Ogerpon formes; therefore, it appreciates aid from Pokemon such as physically defensive Manaphy, Skarmory, and Moltres.

movesets.name: Offensive
movesets.description:
Offensive Great Tusk is an excellent spinner and wallbreaker due to its ability to threaten common spinblockers like Pecharunt and Gholdengo while serving as a great stopgap to the numerous Dark-types the tier has to offer in Kingambit and Roaring Moon. Knock Off is an extremely spammable move that cripples Great Tusk's switch-ins like Zapdos and Moltres, while Head Smash is an excellent option on Magic Guard sets for its ability to let Great Tusk lure in and remove the aforementioned Flying-types. Rapid Spin allows Great Tusk to provide more utility to its team and potentially snowball out of control when also using Bulk Up. Smack Down allows Great Tusk to deal hefty damage to Zapdos and Moltres as well as ground Flying-types like Corviknight, Skarmory, and the Landorus formes, letting it follow up with Headlong Rush. Taunt denies Roost attempts from Great Tusk's checks like Corviknight and Skarmory, Defog from the former, and setup sweepers like IronPress Zamazenta and Swords Dance Kingambit from setting up. Leftovers provides Great Tusk with much-needed longevity, Earth Plate allows Headlong Rush to 2HKO physically defensive Manaphy after mild chip damage, and Life Orb should exclusively be used with Magic Guard to gain a boost on all of Great Tusk's moves that has no drawbacks. Mold Breaker allows Great Tusk to bypass abilities that would hinder it from its checks like Fluffy Corviknight and Skarmory and Levitate or Earth Eater Gholdengo and Iron Hands. Scrappy allows Great Tusk to guarantee a Rapid Spin even in the face of would-be spinblockers while giving it an immunity to Intimidate, making Intimidate Corviknight and Skarmory much shakier checks to it. Magic Guard allows it to ignore passive chip damage and thus boosts its longevity, allowing it to switch in more consistently throughout a game without fear.

Offensive Great Tusk fits best on offensive and bulky offense teams that appreciate its ability to stave off common anti-offense threats like Swords Dance Kingambit and Choice Scarf Roaring Moon while being able to consistently remove entry hazards. Great Tusk dreads special attackers and thus requires good specially defensive partners like RegenVest Roaring Moon, Manaphy, and Swampert. Great Tusk is unable to check many physical threats that can hit it super effectively like the Ogerpon formes and Chien-Pao, making secondary physical walls like Intimidate Pecharunt and the aforementioned Manaphy good teammates. Other physical wallbreakers that appreciate Great Tusk's ability to break through Pecharunt and Fluffy Corviknight and Skarmory, like Zamazenta, Roaring Moon, and Kingambit, pair well with it.

movesets.name: Choice Band
movesets.description:
Great Tusk's powerful STAB moves, massive attack stat, and Choice Band make it one of the strongest wallbreakers in the tier. Knock Off cripples Moltres and Zapdos by removing their Heavy-Duty Boots while helping to make progress against Corviknight and opposing Great Tusk by removing Rocky Helmet or Leftovers. It is also required on Sword of Ruin sets to hit Earth Eater Ghost-types such as Gholdengo and Pecharunt. Ice Spinner handles Flying-types like Zapdos and the Landorus formes that Great Tusk would otherwise struggle with, and Rapid Spin provides useful entry hazard control. Mold Breaker lets Great Tusk completely ignore Earth Eater on the aforementioned Gholdengo and Pecharunt, as well as bypassing Fluffy on Corviknight, Skarmory, and opposing Great Tusk. Sword of Ruin trades these matchups for more power, notably letting Great Tusk potentially 2HKO Corviknight through Intimidate.

Choice Band Great Tusk works best on offense and balance teams, where other physical attackers can make up for its subpar Speed and take advantage of weakened physically defensive walls. Great Tusk can tailor its ability to the team's need, such as running Sword of Ruin when paired with Chien-Pao, thus being able to break past Corviknight regardless of whether it has Intimidate or Fluffy. Similarly, Choice Band Zamazenta can handle Intimidate Corviknight, while Mold Breaker Great Tusk helps threaten both Fluffy Corviknight and Pecharunt. Due to its low Speed and Special Defense, Great Tusk is vulnerable to special attackers such as Latios, Deoxys, and Scream Tail; special walls like Manaphy, Iron Treads, and Swampert can check these threats while also pivoting Great Tusk in.

strategies.overview:
Draft Order: Round 1 onwards

Price Range: 19 points

Overview: In terms of role compression, Great Tusk is excellent for its ability to be versatile in any given matchup. It is primarily used for its ability to control entry hazards, which is a role that is difficult to find given most Pokemon tend to be unreliable. Great Tusk also excels at being able to exert strong offensive pressure, which, alongside Booster Energy and its wide coverage, makes it a constant threat to your opponent's team. Finally, its bulk allows it to check strong physical threats, which can be difficult to handle given how easy it is for most Pokemon in the format can threaten to win the game on the spot. That said, Great Tusk can struggle taking special attacks due to it not having good Special Defense, so it's often pressured by strong special attackers or by Pokemon running special coverage moves to hit its weak point.
strategies.comments:
Common Roles

Offensive Utility: Great Tusk's utility lies in its ability to control entry hazards. By using Stealth Rock and Rapid Spin, it is able to control the field due to its ability to pressure opposing hazard setters and find opportunities to spin. Additionally, it can utilize other moves such as Knock Off and Taunt to facilitate the effectiveness of hazards.

Tank: With its amazing bulk, Great Tusk can be built to take on strong offensive threats that would normally be difficult to check. It doesn't have to worry about compromising its offensive potential, since it has good natural Attack to hit these offensive threats back. In extreme cases, it can use Roar to phaze Pokemon that are difficult to handle.

Setup Sweeper: Mid- or late-game, Great Tusk can clean up opposing teams, using either Rapid Spin or Booster Energy to immediately gain Speed. It can utilize Bulk Up to bolster its offense even further, though oftentimes it can win the game through its strong Attack and coverage. When using Booster Energy for Speed, keep in mind that Great Tusk is lacking in any attacking power due to the need to run maximum Speed and bulk, meaning that it's reliant on either Bulk Up or a very weakened opposing team to effectively win the game.

Wallbreaker: Great Tusk can maximize its offensive potential to break through defensive cores early-game. By using its strong coverage options alongside items such as Choice Band and Booster Energy to bolster its Attack, it can heavily weaken these bulky Pokemon for its teammates that struggle to get past them.

Common Moves

Primary STAB Moves: Headlong Rush, Earthquake, Close Combat, Body Press

Setup Moves: Bulk Up

Utility Moves: Stealth Rock, Taunt, Roar, Knock Off, Rapid Spin, Brick Break

Coverage: Head Smash, Heavy Slam, Ice Spinner, Megahorn, Play Rough, Stone Edge, Temper Flame, Supercell Slam, Zen Headbutt

Niche Moves

Substitute: Substitute can be useful for catching a pivot to scout for information and providing a safeguard against attacks.

Bulldoze / Rock Tomb: These moves can useful for speed control against faster Pokemon and preventing setup sweepers from accumulating Speed boosts to win the game on the spot.

Common Items

Heavy-Duty Boots: Heavy-Duty Boots allows Great Tusk to function well against entry hazards, which it will often need to come in and remove.

Booster Energy: Booster Energy can be used to either give Great Tusk a brief but strong boost to its offensive capabilities or enable it to clean mid- or late-game.

Leftovers: Leftovers give Great Tusk longevity that allows it to consistently switch into attacks, which can be crucial in ensuring its survival.

Rocky Helmet: Rocky Helmet capitalizes on Great Tusk's physical bulk to better punish strong physical attackers.

Niche Items

Assault Vest: Assault Vest allows Great Tusk to check special attackers, which would normally be its main weak point.

Resistance Berry: Resistance Berries can allow Great Tusk to check counters that would normally be difficult to handle. Examples include Roseli Berry for Moonblast Iron Valiant and Coba Berry for Hurricane Zapdos.

Sitrus Berry: Sitrus Berry is good for fast-paced games where Great Tusk needs to check immediate threats.

Choice Scarf: Choice Scarf serves an alternative option for Speed that doesn't make Great Tusk worry about wasting Booster Energy and can let it outspeed immediate threats.

Choice Band: Choice Band maximizes Great Tusk's offensive output to break through sturdy walls.

Eject Pack: Eject Pack takes advantage of Great Tusk's strongest STAB moves by unleashing its attacks and immediately pivoting out to its other partners.

Lum Berry: Lum Berry can be useful on Great Tusk to protect from any status affliction that could prevent it from setting up.

Tera

Great Tusk isn't reliant on Terastallization due to its already good typing, and using it can take away the opportunity of utilizing Terastallization on a more useful Pokemon. That said, it does see experimentation due to its ability to be flexible with its sets and the cost of it Terastallizing being negligible. In terms of useful Tera types, Tera Fairy, Electric, and Ghost are good on offensive sets focused on its setup capabilities, while Tera Steel, Poison, and Water can help against its weaknesses and provide more defensive utility.

Draft Strategy

Great Tusk is usually a high priority to get early in the drafting phase for its ability to compress roles. It is a great starting point that allows you to flesh out your draft and cover what you need.

Fast Pokemon: Having good fast options means not relying on Booster Energy and Rapid Spin for speed control on Great Tusk. Pokemon such as Darkrai, Roaring Moon, and Greninja have great Speed which, alongside benefiting from Great Tusk's wallbreaking power, can allow them to clean up the remaining Pokemon on the opposing team.

Entry Hazard Setters: Employing different means of setting up Stealth Rock releases Great Tusk's burden of having to be the mandatory setter. Examples of other hazard setters include Pokemon such as Mesprit, Glimmora, and Metagross, which can be versatile in support for their ability to provide other utility outside of hazards.

Setup Sweeper: While Great Tusk can be a strong wincon due to its ability to setup, oftentimes you want it either act as a wallbreaker or have it healthy for defensively checking threats. Therefore, having good setup sweepers like Roaring Moon, Dragonite, and Iron Crown can be beneficial for capitalizing on Great Tusk's wallbreaking and ability to find setup opportunities.

Specially Defensive Pokemon: Since Special Defense is Great Tusk's weakest point, having Pokemon that are able to sponge special attacks will help with having a good defensive core. Pokemon such as Latias, Fezandipidi, and Jirachi have good typing and bulk to make good defensive partners alongside Great Tusk.

Checks and Counters

Ground-immune Pokemon: Ground-immune Pokemon often are able to resist Great Tusk's Fighting-type coverage and switch in effortlessly, making it difficult for Great Tusk to spam its STAB moves without potentially letting them in for free. It needs to be wary of Pokemon such as Zapdos, Tornadus-T, and Latias in order to not let them gain momentum.

Ghost-type Pokemon: Ghost-type Pokemon can switch into Great Tusk's Fighting-type coverage and Rapid Spin, which are its common moves. Rotom, Gholdengo, and Pecharunt can be annoying, especially if the latter two use Air Balloon to effectively hard wall its STAB moves. They can also utilize Colbur Berry to weaken the power of Knock Off, which is often Great Tusk's only mean of hitting Ghost-types. Tera Ghost also needs to be kept in mind given how commonly it's used as a Tera type to block Rapin Spin and, by proxy, how difficult it can be for Great Tusk to play around.

Special Attackers: Great Tusk takes severe damage from special attacks. Tornadus-T, Iron Valiant, Enamorus are among the plethora of strong special attackers that Great Tusk needs to be wary of, given it's often slower. It also needs to keep in mind of surprise mixed attackers that utilize strong special coverage to target its weak point, such as Draco Meteor Garchomp and Steel Beam Iron Treads.

Status Conditions: Status conditions can be detrimental to Great Tusk's ability to function. A burn weakens its offensive capability, and poison can gradually weaken it over time, affecting its ability to tank attacks. Great Tusk also needs to be wary of abilities that activate on contact such as Flame Body, Static, and Poison Point due to it often using Close Combat and Knock Off to attack.

movesets.name: Pinsirite
movesets.description: Pinsirite Great Tusk cements itself as the metagame's premier entry hazard remover while also being a respectable offensive threat. Body Slam potentially cripples common switch-ins like Arceus-Water and Latiasite Pecharunt with paralysis. Bulk Up makes Great Tusk a formidable cleaner that's difficult to revenge kill, especially in conjunction with Rapin Spin. Smack Down can be used over Body Slam or Bulk Up to threaten Ground-immune targets such as Latiasite variants of Magearna and Pecharunt as well as Corviknight and Ho-Oh. 204 Speed EVs allow Pinsirite Great Tusk to outspeed Hearthflame Mask Great Tusk, while 144 HP EVs enable it to survive two maximum Attack Altarianite Dragonite Extreme Speeds after Stealth Rock. Strong wallbreakers such as Urshifu-R, Hisuian Arcanine, Raging Bolt, Entei, and Iron Moth benefit from Great Tusk's ability to remove hazards, potentially giving them more opportunities to hit the field. Defensive staples like Garganacl, Pecharunt, and bulky variants of Arceus-Water and Arceus-Fairy also appreciate it removing hazards and maximizing their longevity. Great Tusk struggles against Arceus-Water and Latiasite users like Magearna, so pairing it with answers such as Ho-Oh, Hisuian Arcanine, and Entei for Magearna as well as Eternatus and Raging Bolt for Arceus-Water is crucial. Great Tusk also appreciates specially bulky teammates such as Magearna and Garganacl because special attackers, especially Ice Beam users like Lunala, are troublesome for it.

movesets.name: Stealth Rock
movesets.description: Hearthflame Mask Great Tusk is a fantastic entry hazard setter thanks to Hearthflame Mask providing Mold Breaker, which ignores all Magic Bounce stones being used while also punishing teams that use said ability as their only form of entry hazard control. Knock Off allows Great Tusk to rid switch-ins such as Ho-Oh and Lunala of their Heavy-Duty Boots. Head Smash still handles Ho-Oh while also 2HKOing Sablenite Mandibuzz at the cost of recoil damage. Stone Edge is a slightly weaker option that doesn't wear down Great Tusk as fast; however, it misses out on some key benchmarks, such as 2HKOing Sablenite Mandibuzz. Ice Spinner rounds out Great Tusk's coverage, nailing opposing Ground-types such as non-Hearthflame Mask Great Tusk and Arceus-Ground. Temper Flare is an alternative for a secondary STAB move that nails Corviknight specifically. Rapid Spin can also be slotted in the last slot as emergency hazard control; however, due to lacking an -ate ability, this set struggles to be a reliable spinner. Hearthflame Mask Great Tusk pairs extremely well with more offensive behemoths such as Metagrossite Urshifu-R and Raging Bolt thanks to its Fairy resistance, which lets it handle the likes of Magearna and Altarianite Hisuian Arcanine, and ability to provide chip damage for the aforementioned threats to achieve better benchmarks when aiming to KO the foe. Furthermore, Urshifu-R can threaten Ground-types such as opposing Great Tusk and Arceus-Ground, while Raging Bolt can handle the Water-types that threaten Great Tusk such as Arceus-Water and opposing Urshifu-R. Other good partners include specially defensive walls like Lunala, Garganacl, and Magearna, as they can shore up Great Tusk's weaker defensive stat and form a nice defensive core alongside Great Tusk.

movesets.name: Rusted Sword
movesets.description: Rusted Sword Great Tusk is an incredibly powerful wallbreaker and sweeper thanks to its strong STAB moves in Headlong Rush and Behemoth Blade (Iron Head turns into Behemoth Blade upon switch-in), along with Intrepid Sword. It also offers great utility, with access to Rapid Spin and Stealth Rock. Great Tusk can also forgo Stealth Rock for Bulk Up to become a far more devastating sweeper or instead use a wide range of coverage moves such as Ice Spinner, Stone Edge, and Supercell Slam. Great Tusk fits especially well on hyper offense teams, where it can not only support its teammates by keeping entry hazards off the field while setting its own but also apply heavy offensive pressure as a lead. Great Tusk struggles against common Water-types such as Urshifu-R, Hisuian Samurott, and Arceus-Water; thus, teammates like Dragonite, Regieleki, and Raging Bolt help cover these weaknesses while further applying pressure against the opposing team. In return, Great Tusk helps check common Extreme Speed users, particularly those with Altarianite, that threaten the aforementioned Pokemon thanks to its Steel typing and STAB Behemoth Blade. Setup sweepers, such as Spectrier, Calm Mind Arceus formes, and the aforementioned Dragonite, greatly benefit from the hazard support that Great Tusk provides. Similarly, offensive pivots like Regieleki, Barraskewda, Raging Bolt, and Iron Crown force constant switches from foes, helping to rack up damage from Stealth Rock. Great Tusk can also be used on rain teams, where it more easily withstands Fire-type attacks from threats like Eternatus, Ho-Oh, and Entei. This makes Pelipper a great partner, providing both weather support and the ability to handle Ground- and Fighting-types such as opposing Great Tusk and Metagrossite Urshifu-R. Other Water-type attackers, such as Greninja and Basculegion, also pair well with Great Tusk, as they can also handle Ground-type foes like Arceus-Ground and opposing Great Tusk while also benefiting greatly from the rain.

movesets.name: Speed Booster
movesets.description:
• By using the Speed boost from Booster Energy, Great Tusk is able to outspeed Pokemon such as Meowscarada, Dragapult, Chien-Pao, and Spectrier.
  • Headlong Rush deals with Pokemon like Metagross and Iron Hands.
  • Close Combat is for Dark-type Pokemon such as Urshifu-S, Chien-Pao, Meowscarada, and Darkrai.
  • Bulk Up allows Great Tusk to set up and win against Pokemon such as Metagross and Ursaluna while also improving the chances to win against Pokemon like Pecharunt and Annihilape.
  • Megahorn is used for Hoopa-U, and it can be used to OHKO Ogerpon-W after a Bulk Up. Alternatively, Knock Off can be used to deal with Spectrier, offensive Dragapult, and Pokemon with Chople Berry such as Urshifu-S and Hisuian Goodra. Great Tusk can also run Ice Spinner for a guaranteed win against both Landorus formes and Garchomp. Taunt is also a viable option for better odds against Corviknight, Pecharunt, and stall Pokemon in general.
  • The EV spread gives Great Tusk the Speed boost from Booster Energy and the maximum possible Attack while letting it survive an Overheat from Modest Heatran.
  • While this set outspeeds most threats in the tier, it lacks the power to secure KOs against most bulky Pokemon like Raging Bolt and Volcanion; it also struggles against Fairy- and Water-type Pokemon like Sylveon, Primarina, Manaphy, and Walking Wake. Therefore, Pokemon like Hisuian Goodra, Metagross, Hoopa-U, and Iron Crown that can make up for Great Tusk's low initial power and low Special Defense are great partners for it.

movesets.name: Choice Band
movesets.description:
• Choice Band Great Tusk takes advantage of its unique typing and offensive power to deal great amount of damage to foes like Iron Hands, Roaring Moon, and Diancie.
  • Headlong Rush's damage gives Great Tusk better chances against foes like non-Weakness Policy Primarina if it's lacking Supercell Slam; if it doesn't have Heavy Slam, the move also has a chance to OHKO Sylveon and maximum Defense Diancie.
  • Earthquake is an alternative to Headlong Rush that, despite making Great Tusk lose some matchups due to the lack of immediate power, helps against the Roaring Moon matchup if it's lacking Ice Spinner.
  • Close Combat OHKOes Ursaluna and non-Chople Berry Urshifu-S.
  • Megahorn is for defensive Ogerpon-W and slower Hoopa-U.
  • Ice Spinner OHKOes Landorus-T, Garchomp, and Roaring Moon.
  • Supercell Slam targets Water-types like non-Weakness Policy Primarina.
  • Heavy Slam may be used for Diancie and Sylveon.
  • The EV spread allows Great Tusk to tank a Power Whip from Jolly Ogerpon-W and outspeed Raging Bolt.
  • Headlong Rush is a better option than Close Combat against foes like Hisuian Goodra, since it is able to defeat Great Tusk with the combination of Chople Berry + Counter.
  • Against Corviknight, Close Combat is preferred against Agility or faster variants. Supercell Slam is better suited for slower, bulkier sets.
  • Great Tusk often struggles against Fairy-type foes like Alolan Ninetales and Iron Valiant; therefore, teammates like Volcanion and Metagross are appreciated.

movesets.name: Offensive Utility
movesets.description:
Great Tusk is a behemoth of role compression. It provides an imposing offensive presence, access to entry hazards and hazard removal, and a defensive profile that enables it to check certain physical attackers such as Kingambit and Mega Tyranitar all in one slot. Rapid Spin enables the removal of hazards in the face of nearly every hazard setter in the tier such as Heatran, Garchomp, and Ting-Lu, which is specially given the difficulty of spinblocking Great Tusk, which is able to threaten massive damage on Gholdengo and Pecharunt. Additionally, Ice Spinner is necessary for threatening Flying-types such as Landorus-T, Gliscor, and Zapdos. Great Tusk is a good Stealth Rock setter given its ability to force switches against foes such as Galarian Slowking and Gholdengo and to threaten removal options such as Landorus-T and opposing Great Tusk if carrying Icium Z. Close Combat can be run to deny Ogerpon-W a safe switch in and better pressure Skarmory, Corviknight, and Rotom-W. Alternatively, Knock Off is an option for making progress against Great Tusk's checks, such as through removing Heavy-Duty Boots from Alomomola, Moltres, and Zapdos, as well as hitting Air Balloon Gholdengo for more damage. Stone Edge OHKOes Moltres and Volcarona, as well as 2HKOes Zapdos without making contact. Heavy-Duty Boots protects Great Tusk from Spikes and particularly Toxic Spikes, which is important given its role as hazard removal. Leftovers is another source of longevity, providing passive recovery for longer matchups in exchange for increased vulnerability to offensive hazard pressure. Booster Energy makes Great Tusk nigh unwallable, enabling it to threaten 2HKOs on standard Alomomola, Corviknight, and Rotom-W with its STAB options. Booster Energy sets should always carry Close Combat to maximize wallbreaking potential. Subzero Slammer lets Great Tusk OHKO Tornadus-T and Zapdos, as well as Landorus-T even after Intimidate, while weakening the effect of Knock Off from the likes of Kingambit and Mega Tyranitar. Finally, Rocky Helmet provides a source of chip damage against the physical attackers Great Tusk switches into, including punishing U-turn from pivots such as Landorus-T and Mega Scizor.

Great Tusk's ability to perform a plethora of roles leads it to fit best on offense and bulky offense due to its lack of longevity. However, it is also effective on balance teams, especially with the right teammates such as Alomomola, as its traits are highly coveted nonetheless. Great Tusk is often forced out by special attackers, such as Tapu Lele and Mega Charizard Y, meaning teammates such as Melmetal and Toxapex are strong teammates. Great Tusk is also not a blanket check to physical attackers, as its somewhat double-edged defensive typing leaves it with common weaknesses to attacks from Ogerpon-W, Weavile, and Kartana. As a result, defensive Pokemon with complementary typings such as Ferrothorn and Alomomola are effective partners. In particular, the latter can also provide Great Tusk with Wish support to mitigate its lack of longevity. With regards to its offensive profile, Great Tusk appreciates the ability of powerful special wallbreakers such as Raging Bolt and Tapu Lele to break through its checks such as Alomomola and Skarmory. In return, Great Tusk can exploit their checks such as Ting-Lu, Ferrothorn, and Melmetal as opportunities to set up Stealth Rock or remove entry hazards with ease. On offense teams, Great Tusk can pair well with other physical attackers such as Kingambit and Swords Dance Iron Valiant, being able to overwhelm or threaten common switch-ins such as Landorus-T and Moltres. Finally, Great Tusk forms a powerful core with Mega Charizard Y, providing premium hazard removal to address its crippling Stealth Rock weakness, the ability to switch into powerful physical attackers such as Mega Tyranitar, and threatening Mega Charizard Y's checks such as Dragonite, Toxapex, and Raging Bolt. In exchange, Mega Charizard Y's Drought provides Great Tusk with a Protosynthesis boost at no cost to the item slot while using Great Tusk's switch-ins such as Alomomola and Slowbro as wallbreaking opportunities.

movesets.name: Defensive
movesets.description:
Defensive Great Tusk acts as important glue on teams due to its incredible role compression by acting as a defensive wall, setting entry hazards, and clearing them. Utilizing its high bulk and HP, defensive Great Tusk acts as a great check to many metagame staples such as all-out attacker Zamazenta, Kingambit, Mega Lopunny, and Mega Tyranitar. Earthquake is the preferred STAB move on Great Tusk, but Headlong Rush can also be run for better damage rolls, such as an OHKO on offensive Gholdengo and a 2HKO on Kartana, at the cost of lowering its defenses. Moreover, Headlong Rush isn't weakened by Grassy Terrain. Ice Spinner is used mainly to threaten Landorus-T, Gliscor, and Dragonite while also hitting Zapdos and opposing Great Tusk super effectively. Great Tusk can freely remove hazards, since spinblockers like Dragapult and Gholdengo are threatened by moves such as Ice Spinner and Earthquake, respectively, and Knock Off. The last slot on this set is flexible; running Stealth Rock turns Great Tusk into an effective hazard setter, threatening most hazard removal options such as Landorus-T and opposing Great Tusk with Ice Spinner. Knock Off can also be run to remove key items, like Heavy-Duty Boots from the likes of Zapdos, Tornadus-T, and Moltres as well as Leftovers from Landorus-T and opposing Great Tusk, with the added benefit of being able to hit Air Balloon Gholdengo and Dragapult super effectively. Body Press is an option in the final slot to surprise Ferrothorn, Ting-Lu, and Terapagos that has had its Tera Shell broken. 40 Speed EVs allow defensive Great Tusk to outspeed base 90s like Moltres as well as other prominent threats such as uninvested Landorus-T and bulky Gholdengo. Heavy-Duty Boots prevents Great Tusk from taking too much chip damage from hazards, while Leftovers helps in checking the threats and increases Great Tusk's longevity. Rocky Helmet is another item that can be run on Great Tusk to punish many physical attackers that either attack it recklessly or try to gain momentum like Landorus-T, Zamazenta, and Kingambit.

Defensive Great Tusk fits best on balance and bulky offense teams, which value its role compression. The main attributes hindering Great Tusk are its typing and lack of longevity. Thus, Great Tusk appreciates partners like Alomomola, which helps with its lack of longevity by Wish passing; additionally, Alomomola is able to switch into common Water-types like Hisuian Samurott and Urshifu-R. It also appreciates Pokemon such as Volt Switch Raging Bolt and Zapdos that can reliably switch in against common Flying-types such as Zapdos, Tornadus-T, and Mega Charizard Y and Water-types like Ogerpon-W while also threatening them offensively. Steel-type partners like Mega Scizor and Melmetal are greatly valued due to their ability to switch into fast Fairy-type foes like Tapu Lele. Moreover, the hazards set up by Great Tusk pressure many switch-ins on entry, forcing progress over time. Being able to remove the items on checks to Raging Bolt like Leftovers from Ting-Lu and Assault Vest from Melmetal allows Raging Bolt to break through switch-ins with its STAB moves aided by Great Tusk's hazards. Furthermore, these teammates appreciate Great Tusk's ability to spin away hazards for them and can continue to check threats to Great Tusk. Defensive Great Tusk also pairs extremely well with Mega Charizard Y, which appreciates Great Tusk removing Stealth Rock and checking Pokemon such as Mega Tyranitar. In return, Mega Charizard Y is able to break through walls like Alomomola, Clefable, Skarmory, and Corviknight. Mega Charizard Y also sets up sun, granting Great Tusk a Defense boost due to Protosynthesis, which allows it to better wall physical attackers.

movesets.name: Bulk Up
movesets.description:
Great Tusk's already great Attack and physical bulk combined with Bulk Up make it a premier setup sweeper that can use its bulk to set up with ease on Pokemon like Dragonite, Garchomp, and Mega Scizor. Ice Spinner takes care of most Pokemon immune to Headlong Rush like Landorus-T, Zapdos, Mega Latios, and Gliscor, among others, while also dealing with Grass-types like Rillaboom and Meowscarada. Rapid Spin is an amazing utility move for Great Tusk, as the extra boosts to Great Tusk's Speed help it avoid revenge killing attempts from Speed Booster Energy Iron Valiant and Choice Scarf Tapu Lele and let it boost Speed after its Booster Energy is used up. Rapid Spin also removes entry hazards for Great Tusk's teammates to clean up after it. The EV spread guarantees Great Tusk gains a Speed boost from its Booster Energy, allowing it to threaten Pokemon it would normally be threatened by, like Mega Diancie, Dragapult, and Mega Medicham.

Bulk Up sets are most commonly used on hyper offense teams that appreciate another setup sweeper that can threaten common Pokemon like Landorus-T, Kingambit, and Raging Bolt for its teammates to cleave through. These teams also appreciate Great Tusk's ability to remove entry hazards, which is extremely helpful for Pokemon like Mega Charizard Y and Z-Move Dragonite. Great Tusk is easily revenge killed by Pokemon like mixed Iron Valiant and Choice Scarf users like Tapu Lele and Urshifu-R even with the Speed boost. Therefore, Pokemon that can switch into these Pokemon such as Mega Scizor for Tapu Lele and Kartana and Dragonite for Urshifu-R are appreciated. Great Tusk is weak to special attackers like the aforementioned Iron Valiant, Tapu Lele, Terapagos, and Volcarona, so Pokemon like Kingambit, Raging Bolt, Roaring Moon and your own Terapagos can be useful. Great Tusk also thuds into Pokemon that can take both of its moves, like Ogerpon-W, Moltres, Slowbro, and Alomomola, so Pokemon like your own Ogerpon-W, Raging Bolt, and Gholdengo are great partners that can chip down these Pokemon for Great Tusk to sweep.

movesets.name: Choice Scarf (Ground)
movesets.description: With a handy dandy Choice Scarf, Great Tusk breaks the threshold of 450 Speed to outspeed threats like Greninja, Latios, and Latias, shifting the sands of the battle. Knock Off is great for removing items from pesky bulky Pokemon like Rocky Helmet on Skarmory and Eject Button on Hippowdon. Ice Spinner helps versus Flying-types like Gliscor, Landorus, and Dragonite while also hitting Mega Altaria for a 2HKO; Great Tusk outspeeds it even after a Dragon Dance. Alternatively, Megahorn can be used to deal with Ogerpon-W, Celebi, Slowbro, and Latios, and Latias, which makes Great Tusk a huge threat versus Psychic teams. Although Great Tusk has all these great attributes, it lacks the bulk that more defensive sets typically run and can be threatened out quite easily by Grass- and Water-types and by special attackers like Keldeo and Greninja. Clodsire makes a good teammate, as it can swap into these threats reliably, sponge hits from them, and provide an effective Water immunity. Clodsire also provides status and entry hazards to assist Great Tusk in cleaning up the competition with reliable chip damage. Hippowdon is a great secondary partner that can sponge damage for Great Tusk and set up sand and hazards for much-needed chip damage. Excadrill, is a secondary physical wallbreaker, utilizing either Swords Dance or Choice Band under sand to check Fairy- and Ice-type threats that Great Tusk can't outspeed like Choice Scarf Tapu Lele and Choice Scarf Galarian Darmanitan with its Steel-type STAB moves. Mamoswine additionally assists as a secondary wallbreaker, as it reliably takes on Flying-type threats that it can OHKO with its powerful Icicle Crash like non-Choice Specs Zapdos and Crobat. Landorus with Gravity helps check Steel / Flying types, assisting Great Tusk by breaking a notable defensive answer. Additionally, Mega Garchomp helps versus Dragon-types while also threatening Steel / Flying types.

movesets.name: Defensive Utility (Fighting)
movesets.description: Great Tusk fills a crucial set of roles on Fighting teams and provides great role compression, being the type's premier Stealth Rock + Rapid Spin user. Knock Off furthers Great Tusk's capabilities, enabling it to remove Heavy-Duty Boots from the likes of Crobat and Zapdos as they both come into Great Tusk's Earthquake and use Defog. Furthermore, Knock Off also allows Great Tusk to hit Ghost-types, such as Air Balloon Gholdengo. Earthquake combined with Great Tusk's Electric immunity and general bulk allows Great Tusk to stop threats such as Regieleki and Mega Charizard X from running through Fighting teams. Taunt can be run as an alternative option over Rapid Spin to prevent threats such as Ting-Lu and Skarmory from setting entry hazards or Defog users like Corviknight from removing Great Tusk's Stealth Rock. Leftovers grants Great Tusk longevity, while Heavy-Duty Boots provides safe entry, allowing it to use Rapid Spin without worrying about hazard damage. The given EV spreads maximize Great Tusk's physical bulk; 120 Speed EVs are preferred to let Great Tusk outspeed Modest Volcanion, but 96 Speed EVs can be used instead to further increase its bulk while still allowing Great Tusk to outspeed threats such as Latios and Iron Moth after a Rapid Spin. Sneasler serves as an excellent teammate with its incredible Speed and Poison typing, enabling it to handle Fairy- and Grass-types, such as Iron Valiant, Tapu Bulu, and Breloom. Iron Valiant can threaten opposing Great Tusk and Dark-types like Sableye and Mandibuzz with Moonblast, allowing for Great Tusk to reliably get Stealth Rock up. Iron Valiant also uses coverage moves such as Thunderbolt to deal with Slowbro and Mega Charizard Y while appreciating Great Tusk's handling of Poison-types, such as Sneasler and Galarian Slowking. Mega Gallade can check Poison- and Fighting-type threats such as Mega Venusaur and Keldeo. Kommo-o appreciates Great Tusk keeping hazards off the field and, in response, can set up safely with Clangorous Soulblaze, enabling it to overcome Flying and Water teams that greatly threaten Great Tusk. Assault Vest Iron Hands can threaten Water- and Flying-types such as Greninja, Pelipper, and Tornadus-T while appreciating Great Tusk's Stealth Rock, enabling it to 2HKO physically defensive Toxapex.

movesets.name: Bulk Up (Ground)
movesets.description: Great Tusk is a deadly wallbreaker on Ground teams, possessing excellent stats, a potent STAB combination, and access to utility moves like Knock Off and Rapid Spin. Close Combat threatens Ice- and Dark-types such as Baxcalibur, Hydreigon, and Hisuian Samurott as well as OHKOing walls like Celesteela, Corviknight, Mega Scizor, and Rotom-W with the aid of Fightinium Z after a Bulk Up boost, easing the Steel matchup for Great Tusk's team. Earthquake hits Pokemon like Skeledirge, Gholdengo, and Toxapex, while Ice Spinner nails Landorus-T, Dragonite, and Zapdos, allowing Great Tusk to boast unresisted coverage in combination with Close Combat. Rapid Spin allows Great Tusk to gain a Speed boost to easily snowball against slower teams and remove entry hazards for teammates; however, Knock Off is great for Air Balloon Gholdengo and weakened Slowbro as well as generally forcing progress against teams by removing their items. Gastrodon and Clodsire are essential teammates for Great Tusk due to their immunities to Water-type attacks, letting them fend off Barraskewda, Urshifu-R, and Keldeo. Gastrodon also has an appreciated neutrality to Ice-type attacks, letting it check Choice Scarf Weavile, and Clodsire is neutral to Grass-type attacks, letting it wall Meowscarada. It can also wall Fairy-types like Tapu Koko, Tapu Fini, and Iron Valiant. Furthermore, Gastrodon and Clodsire provide chip damage via Toxic and entry hazards, wearing down walls like Slowbro, Swampert, and Mantine that give Great Tusk a hard time. Landorus forms a potent wallbreaking core with Great Tusk, breaking Slowbro, Dondozo, and Mandibuzz as well as offering Gravity, letting Great Tusk more easily spam Earthquake. In return, Landorus appreciates Great Tusk threatening Ice Shard users like Mamoswine and Baxcalibur. Mega Steelix is an excellent teammate, as it fights off Azumarill, Weavile, and Alolan Ninetales, making it a huge asset in the Fairy and Ice matchups. Ting-Lu forms an entry hazard-stacking core with Gastrodon and Clodsire, wearing down teams exponentially faster with the help of Whirlwind. Additionally, Ting-Lu switches into attacks from revenge killers like Blacephalon, Latias, and Hisuian Zoroark. Mamoswine appreciates Great Tusk breaking Celesteela and Corviknight; in return, Mamoswine utilizes Thick Fat to fight the aforementioned Ice-types and provides speed control with Choice Scarf, outpacing Mega Diancie, Enamorus, and Tapu Koko. Choice Scarf Iron Treads outpaces and OHKOes the aforementioned Fairy-types, most notably Iron Valiant, and provides pivoting support via Volt Switch.
